A stacked bar chart illustrates emissions reduction from a baseline to final product emissions. 

The first bar is labeled "445 kg" with subtitle "Baseline emissions[note 7]" and consists of four segments from top to bottom: "Materials and process emissions", "Electricity for manufacturing", "Electricity for product use", and "Transportation".

The middle bar is labeled "−99 kg" with subtitle "Emissions reductions". It breaks down the baseline into reductions and remaining emissions. The reduction segments with dashed outlines are "Recycled and low-carbon materials[note 8]", "Low-carbon electricity[note 9]", and "Non-air shipping". The remaining segments are "Materials and process emissions", "Electricity for manufacturing", "Electricity for product use", and "Transportation".

A curved green arrow leads to the third bar, labeled "346 kg" with subtitle "iMac emissions[note 10]". This bar consists of segments from top to bottom: "Materials and process emissions", "Electricity for manufacturing", "Electricity for product use", a thin sliver labeled "Renewable energy emissions[note 11]", and "Transportation".

Individual segments are not labeled with numerical values. The chart demonstrates that 445 kg baseline emissions minus 99 kg emissions reductions equals 346 kg iMac emissions.

A circular life cycle diagram shows five stages linked by clockwise arrows, each with an icon, title, and description:

DESIGN AND SOURCE: Maximize the use of recycled content and responsibly source primary materials.

MAKE: Uphold high standards of labor and human rights, health and safety, and minimizing our environmental impact.

PACKAGE AND SHIP: Remove plastic from our packaging and minimize emissions from transportation.

USE: Minimize emissions from product use, enhance product longevity, and seek to avoid exposure to harmful chemicals.

RECOVER: Reuse products through Apple Trade In and maximize material recovery at end of life.
